description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:930-1028: verify_smime_signer and verify_smime_recipient have BYTE-IDENTICAL function bodies. The rustdoc at line 939-942 says 'The signer-vs-recipient distinction is encoded in the caller-supplied Profile's ValidationPolicy: signer profiles require KeyUsage digitalSignature, recipient profiles require keyEncipherment.' But pkix-profiles ships only BasicSmimeProfile, which sets required_leaf_eku=emailProtection and require_rfc822_san=true — it does NOT set any KU requirement. There is no BasicSmimeSignerProfile / BasicSmimeRecipientProfile. So in practice both wrappers do the same thing for the only shipped profile. Trigger: caller writes verify_smime_recipient(signer_cert_chain, ...) expecting recipient-shape enforcement, gets exactly what verify_smime_signer would have returned, including for a cert with KU=digitalSignature only. Documentation promises a guarantee that the shipped profile does not deliver. Two options: (1) ship BasicSmimeSignerProfile/BasicSmimeRecipientProfile with the documented KU shapes, OR (2) reword the rustdoc to be honest that the distinction is intent-only and the caller must wire a profile that imposes the KU constraint they want. Recommend option (1) so new callers don't have to read this footnote.
title: verify_smime_signer / verify_smime_recipient distinction is documentation-only — no shipped profile enforces it
